# Andrew Rudin, MD

> Andrew Rudin, MD is a cardiologist and board-certified cardiac electrophysiologist. He takes a natural, root-cause approach to heart health and sees telehealth patients nationally and internationally through Natural Heart Doctor.

## Facts

- Name: Andrew Rudin, MD
- Specialty: cardiology and cardiac electrophysiology (heart rhythm, atrial fibrillation)
- Board certification: Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology, American Board of Internal Medicine
- Licensure: Tennessee
- Practice: telehealth consultations and second opinions through Natural Heart Doctor (naturalheartdoctor.com)
- Role: consulting physician. He recommends diet, lifestyle and supplements and works alongside each patient's own prescribing doctor.
- Training: MD, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (1996); internal medicine residency and chief residency, Yale-New Haven Hospital; cardiology and cardiac electrophysiology fellowships, Northwestern Memorial Hospital
- Focus: root causes of heart disease, including insulin resistance, inflammation, sleep, stress, the gut microbiome and environmental toxins

## Articles

- [The Root Causes of High Blood Pressure: Why I No Longer Believe in Essential Hypertension](https://bestheartbeat.com/root-causes-of-high-blood-pressure/): Everyone with high blood pressure has it for a reason. Sleep, insulin resistance, stress and inflammation, the two types I see, and the diet and labs I use.
- [Why AFib Patients Have Higher Rates of Cancer (and What It Tells You About the Cause)](https://bestheartbeat.com/afib-cancer-risk-inflammation/): Every large cohort shows AFib patients get more cancer: +48% in the Women's Health Study, nearly 3x when diagnosed under 50. AFib doesn't cause cancer. They share a root cause.
- [Is Berberine Bad for Your Gut Long Term? A Cardiologist Looks at the Data](https://bestheartbeat.com/berberine-long-term-gut-health/): Influencers say berberine is fine short term but hurts the gut long term. TMAO, LPS, Akkermansia, the PREMOTE trial and a 6-year polyp study say otherwise.
- [Why the Antioxidant Trials Failed (and What They Don&rsquo;t Tell You)](https://bestheartbeat.com/why-antioxidant-trials-failed/): HOPE, HPS, ATBC, SELECT: thousands of patients, no benefit. They tested one isolated molecule, crowded out its cofactors, and never asked what was oxidizing the artery in the first place.
- [Vegan With a Normal CRP? Check Your Oxidative Stress Markers](https://bestheartbeat.com/vegan-oxidative-stress-mda-vs-crp/): Why the vegans I see have a clean CRP but very high urine malondialdehyde, and why oxidized LDL does not need inflammation to build plaque.
- [Lead and Your Heart: Why Normal Isn’t Optimal](https://bestheartbeat.com/lead-and-your-heart/): Lead levels labs call normal were tied to 70% higher cardiovascular death over 19 years. Why I test for lead, cadmium and arsenic.
- [Giving Blood to Lower PFAS: Answering the Objections](https://bestheartbeat.com/pfas-blood-donation-objections/): Are you just passing your PFAS to the recipient? Is this bloodletting? Answers to the top reader objections, plus the test I use.
- [Donating Blood Lowers Forever Chemicals](https://bestheartbeat.com/donating-blood-lowers-pfas/): The 2022 firefighter trial is the only randomized evidence that anything lowers PFAS in humans. Plasma every 6 weeks cut PFOS 30 percent. What that means for a patient with plaque.
- [Why I Never Use Synthetic Vitamins](https://bestheartbeat.com/why-i-never-use-synthetic-vitamins/): A 1951 experiment: rats given every known vitamin quit swimming in 13 minutes; rats fed liver swam for hours. The case for whole-food supplements over isolated vitamins.
- [Can Persistent AFib Convert Without Ablation?](https://bestheartbeat.com/persistent-afib-convert-without-ablation/): An 82-year-old with two years of persistent AFib converted to normal sinus rhythm on a root-cause plan - no ablation, no drugs, no cardioversion. A case from my practice.
- [The Screening Cascade: How a Calcium Scan Becomes a Stent You Never Needed](https://bestheartbeat.com/the-screening-cascade-calcium-scan-to-stent/): A high calcium score often leads to a stress test, a cath, and an elective stent - without improving survival. What the ISCHEMIA trial actually showed.
- [Excess Niacin, NAD Boosters, and Heart Disease Risk](https://bestheartbeat.com/excess-niacin-nad-supplements-heart-risk/): New research links megadosed B3 and &ldquo;NAD boosters&rdquo; (NR, NMN) to vascular inflammation - and what to take instead.
- [Elective Stents vs. Heart-Attack Stents](https://bestheartbeat.com/elective-stents-vs-heart-attack-stents/): One saves lives. The other usually doesn&rsquo;t change them. The distinction every patient should understand before the cath lab.
- [Inflammation and Your Heart: A Root-Cause View](https://bestheartbeat.com/inflammation-and-your-heart-a-root-cause-view/): Why nearly everyone already has some coronary disease - and why inflammation, not just cholesterol, deserves your attention.
